desc:
You may add characters only at the front of the string s; nothing can be inserted in the middle or at the end. Find the shortest palindrome you can create this way and return its length.

For example, for s = "aacecaaa" you can prepend a single a to get "aaacecaaa", so the answer is 9. For s = "abcd" you must prepend "dcb" to get "dcbabcd", so the answer is 7. If s is already a palindrome the answer is len(s).
constraints: s consists of lowercase letters and digits
hints: Whatever you add is determined by how much of the start of s is already a palindrome.
If the longest palindromic prefix of s has length k, the remaining n - k characters must be mirrored in front, so the answer is 2n - k.

Find k in linear time with the KMP prefix function on s + '#' + reverse(s): the last value of the prefix function is the length of the longest prefix of s that equals a suffix of reverse(s), i.e. a palindromic prefix.
editorial: Let k be the length of the longest prefix of s that is a palindrome. The characters after that prefix cannot be part of the palindromic core, so their reverse must be placed in front, giving a result of length n + (n - k) = 2n - k. Any shorter result would need a longer palindromic prefix, contradicting maximality of k.

Checking every prefix for palindromicity costs O(n²), acceptable only for small inputs. To get O(n), build t = s + '#' + reverse(s) and compute the KMP failure (prefix) function. The final value pi[-1] is exactly k: a prefix of s that matches a suffix of reverse(s) is a prefix that equals its own reversal. The separator keeps the match from crossing the boundary (the alphabet never contains #).
